query: For a FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy alloy used as a thin coating on a conventional metal substrate, what single testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs overall wear resistance and microscopic deformation during sliding in the intended high-temperature operating regime? Define a controlled change relative to a baseline coating condition, predict the corresponding directional changes in wear and deformation, state the regime in which those predictions should hold, identify supporting prior evidence, and specify a result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: The wear resistance and microscopic deformation of a FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy alloy thin coating on a conventional metal substrate during high-temperature sliding are governed by the formation of a stable, coherent oxide layer at the surface, which acts as a sacrificial layer to reduce metal-to-metal contact and associated wear.
generation.material_initial_state: FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy alloy thin coating on a conventional metal substrate, with a surface roughness of 0.1 μm and a coating thickness of 10 μm
generation.intervention: In-situ high-temperature sliding wear tests with a controlled change in oxygen partial pressure (pO2) from 10^-5 to 10^-3 atm, and a corresponding change in surface oxide layer thickness from 100 to 500 nm
generation.conditions: High-temperature sliding wear tests conducted at 800°C, with a sliding speed of 0.1 m/s and a normal load of 10 N
generation.structural_mediator: Stable, coherent oxide layer at the surface of the FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy alloy thin coating
generation.mechanism: Formation of a sacrificial oxide layer that reduces metal-to-metal contact and associated wear, through a combination of oxidation and wear-induced surface modification
generation.predicted_outcome: A 30% increase in wear resistance and a 25% reduction in microscopic deformation, relative to a baseline coating condition with a surface oxide layer thickness of 100 nm
generation.baseline: FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy alloy thin coating with a surface oxide layer thickness of 100 nm, tested under the same high-temperature sliding wear conditions
generation.boundary: High-temperature sliding wear regime, with temperatures between 700°C and 900°C, and sliding speeds between 0.01 and 1 m/s
generation.uncertainty: The exact composition and structure of the surface oxide layer, and the potential for other wear mechanisms to contribute to the overall wear resistance and deformation

falsification_experiment.design: In-situ high-temperature sliding wear tests with a controlled change in oxygen partial pressure (pO2) and surface oxide layer thickness, using a combination of experimental and simulation approaches to validate and refine mechanistic hypotheses
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the wear rate and microscopic deformation do not decrease by at least 20% with an increase in surface oxide layer thickness from 100 to 500 nm, then the hypothesis is falsified

limitation.phenomenon: governing mechanisms of wear resistance and deformation during sliding at high temperatures

prior_attempts.shortcoming: lack of mechanistic understanding of wear resistance and deformation
